triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: the pre-fix capped the dependent's deduction at single_basic_standard_deduction and declared the rule on entity Person, whereas 63(c)(5) limits 'the basic standard deduction applicable to such individual' (whatever that individual's own filing status is) — but the pre-fix module openly declared that choice in its summary and its indexed $1,350/$450 amounts are defensible under 63(c)(4), so the evidence does not settle that the pre-fix was wrong.
triage.triage_notes: Provision READ via resolve_provision: 63(c)(5) reads 'the basic standard deduction applicable to such individual for such individual's taxable year shall not exceed the greater of— (A) $500, or (B) the sum of $250 and such individual's earned income.' Pre-fix summary explicitly said 'subject to the single-filer basic standard deduction' and 'Annual inflation-adjusted dollar amounts are imported from the IRS tax-year authority, not encoded in the statute file', so the single-filer ceiling was a deliberate, documented choice rather than an obvious slip; that plus the fact that the fix replaces indexed $1,350/$450 with unindexed statutory $500/$250 (dropping the 63(c)(4) adjustment this module used to get from the Rev. Proc.) is why I kept this unclear rather than fidelity. Real changes in the diff: entity Person -> TaxUnit, the min() ceiling moved out into 63/c.yaml where it is now taken against the taxpayer's own basic standard deduction, and a new Judgment rule for the 'deduction under section 151 allowable to another taxpayer' condition. Same encoder-rewrite pattern as index 5.
triage.verifier_justification: The only defensible fidelity element in this file is scope: the pre-fix capped the dependent at `single_basic_standard_deduction` regardless of the individual's own filing status, while 63(c)(5) limits "the basic standard deduction applicable to such individual", and the post-state's parent (statutes/26/63/c.yaml) now applies `min(basic_standard_deduction_before_dependent_limitation, dependent_basic_standard_deduction_statutory_limit)`, which is filing-status aware — so a HoH dependent with ~$20k earned income moves from $16,100 to $20,450. But I cannot confirm, because the same diff moves the amounts the wrong way: it replaces the imported 2026 indexed values ($1,350 / $450, Rev. Proc. 2025-32 §.14(2)) with the raw statutory 500 / 250 under an `effective_from: '2026-01-01'` version, and the pinned corpus text of 63(c)(4) indexes "each dollar amount contained in paragraph (2)(B), (2)(C), or (5)" with (7)(B)(i) suspending paragraph (4) only for (2)(B) and (2)(C) — so paragraph (5) stays indexed and $500 is wrong for 2026. The commit's own new test locks that in (`dependent_with_no_earned_income_uses_floor` → statutory_limit 500 for TY2026) and the still-correct rev-proc `dependent_standard_deduction_floor_amount: 1350` is now orphaned from the 63(c) chain. Given a generic message ("Encode upstream IRC 63 dependencies" / "encode 26 USC 63(c) standard deduction through the encoder apply flow") and a wholesale re-encode that corrects one scope narrowing while introducing an amount regression, the evidence does not settle this as a fidelity fix.
triage.verifier_notes: Recommend a reviewer prune or heavily caveat this case. Evidence gathered: (1) entity change `-    entity: Person` → `+    entity: TaxUnit` moves AWAY from the statute's "an individual" and is structural alignment with the TaxUnit-scoped consumer, so the "entity" half of wrong_entity_or_scope is not supported by the source; only the filing-status ("scope") half is. (2) The corrective effect of dropping the single-filer ceiling is realized in a different file (statutes/26/63/c.yaml, module index 5), not in this one — this file merely stops computing a ceiling and is renamed from `dependent_standard_deduction` (the deduction) to `dependent_basic_standard_deduction_statutory_limit` (the cap), an output-surface redefinition. (3) The pre-fix summary openly declared the simplification ("subject to the single-filer basic standard deduction"), and its $1,350/$450 were correct for 2026. (4) The post-fix introduces a fresh fidelity defect (amount_mismatch / unrepresented 63(c)(4) indexation) in the same hunk — this would be a better corpus case in the reverse direction, i.e. as a defect INTRODUCED at 86e2549dc7, if the corpus ever wants regression examples. Verified against the pinned release us-rulespec-2026-07-13 (corpus commit 612d20ca43), citation us/statute/26/63.
